Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Aether Dynamics Fourth Quarter and Full-Year 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Aether Dynamics' Fourth Quarter and Full-Year 2023 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Mark Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; John Ellis, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Technology Officer; and David Patel, Chief Strategy Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those statements.

Mark Harlan:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Aether Dynamics delivered a solid performance in the fourth quarter and full year 2023, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across aeronautics, missiles, space, and beyond. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering compelling value to our shareholders. We're particularly excited about the recent advancements in our F-47 Lightning II program and its potential to solidify our leadership in next-generation multirole fighters critical for air dominance. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, from hypersonics to integrated air defenses, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily amid production ramps.

I'll now turn it over to Sarah for a deep dive into our financial results and key performance areas.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Mark, and good morning, everyone. I'm delighted to walk you through our financial results, starting with what I can confidently describe as a banner year—one that highlights our resilience, execution discipline, and strategic positioning in the Aerospace & Defense sector against a backdrop of evolving geopolitical dynamics.

Let me lead with the top-line figures that capture our momentum. For the full year 2023, we achieved record consolidated revenues of $24.7 billion, reflecting a 14% increase year-over-year and surpassing our guidance midpoint by $400 million. This robust growth stemmed from a book-to-bill ratio of 1.28x, which built to a record backlog of $158 billion by year-end—up 18% from 2022 and offering outstanding multi-year revenue visibility. Adjusted EPS reached $12.45, marking a strong 22% rise from the prior year, propelled by elevated volumes, a favorable program mix, and 220 basis points of segment operating margin expansion to 13.8%. Free cash flow stood out at $3.2 billion, equivalent to 13% of revenues, which supported $1.8 billion in share repurchases, a 12% increase in our dividend to $3.20 per share, and $750 million deployed toward strategic tuck-in acquisitions.

By segment, our Aeronautics unit—driven by cornerstone programs like the F-47 Lightning II multirole fighter and our next-generation trainer comparable to the T-7A Red Hawk—generated $9.8 billion in revenues, up 16%, as margins grew 180 basis points to 12.5%. Deliveries under low-rate initial production Lot 16 picked up pace with supply chain stabilization, and we captured a $5.2 billion Foreign Military Sales contract for 48 aircraft to NATO partners such as Poland and Finland. Meanwhile, our sixth-generation fighter demonstrator, tailored to NGAD requirements, achieved pivotal milestones in digital twin validation, cutting engineering hours by 25% through model-based systems engineering approaches.

Missiles & Fire Control brought in $8.1 billion in revenues, a 12% year-over-year gain, supported by heightened demand for hypersonic weapons and precision-guided munitions like JASSM-ER and our LRASM equivalent, ramping to 1,200 units per year. Margins climbed to 15.2%—an improvement of 250 basis points—due to efficiencies in fixed-price contracts and progress on directed energy weapon prototypes moving into engineering and manufacturing development. Geopolitical pressures in the Indo-Pacific and Europe lifted international orders by 30%, highlighted by a $2.8 billion agreement for integrated air defense systems with Saudi Arabia and Australia.

Our Space Systems segment posted $6.8 billion in revenues, rising 15%, led by satellite constellations and launch vehicles echoing Starliner and Orion capabilities. The Polaris reusable booster notched its third successful orbital test, reducing launch costs by 40% compared to expendable options, while our protected communications payload for the US Space Force's PLEO program shifted to full-rate production. Margins rose to 11.9%, aided by commercial hyperspectral imaging efforts accessing the $12 billion NewSpace market.

On the operational side, we managed inflation challenges—especially in titanium and rare earths—via our Resilient Supply Chain 2.0 program, which localized 65% of critical subsystems using US-based 3D printing and AI-enhanced inventory controls. This delivered $450 million in cost savings compared to the prior year, alongside an 18% boost in labor productivity from digital thread deployments in our facilities. ESG efforts advanced with a 25% drop in Scope 1 emissions through sustainable aviation fuel tests on our test fleet, putting us ahead of DoD requirements.

Geographically, US government sales—at 85% of our total—advanced 13%, tracking the FY24 NDAA's $886 billion headline. International revenues jumped 22% to $4.2 billion, with EMEA up 28% from Ukraine-driven FMS urgency and APAC up 19% amid Taiwan Strait dynamics and AUKUS Pillar II work. Emerging markets like India added via offset deals on Tejas Mk2 co-production.

Strategically, we concentrated on three core pillars: innovation leadership in autonomy and hypersonics, backed by $1.2 billion in R&D that produced 15 new patents in quantum-secured communications; portfolio shaping, including divesting non-core legacy avionics for $300 million to finance AI/ML autonomy platforms; and capital deployment aiming for 10-12% ROIC, with M&A capacity for electronic warfare adjacencies.

Key takeaways here: our $158 billion backlog secures over four years of revenues with double-digit growth; margin expansion to 13.8% validates our pricing discipline and cost controls despite inflation; geopolitical tailwinds—from Ukraine logistics to China deterrence—set us up for 10-12% organic growth over the decade; and with FY24 guidance at $26.0-27.0 billion in revenues, $13.50-14.00 adjusted EPS, and $3.5 billion in free cash flow, we're elevating expectations while upholding investment-grade balance sheet strength.

With that foundation, let's examine our program margins and cost performance in greater depth. In Q4, segment-wide adjusted program margins grew 90 basis points year-over-year to 11.2%, from 10.3% a year earlier, marking three straight quarters of progress. This came from transitions to higher-margin full-rate production phases on major efforts, partially counterbalanced by development-related pressures. Segment revenue climbed 8% to $4.2 billion, with book-to-bill at 1.15x, signaling solid demand from US DoD and global clients.

In Defense Fixed-Wing, about 45% of segment revenue, the NGAD demonstrator excelled with a CPI of 1.05 and SPI of 1.02, holding margins at 13.5%—above our 12% long-term goal—owing to digital twins and model-based systems engineering that trimmed engineering change order costs by 15%. Year-to-date funded deliveries totaled $1.8 billion, with LRIP Lot 3 fully funded under a fixed-price incentive structure sharing upside.

For rotary-wing, MH-60R Seahawk sustainment akin to Sikorsky's global reach expanded margins to 12.8% from 11.9%, via volume leverage from FMS to Australia and India. We absorbed $45 million in cost growth on Future Vertical Lift prototypes from titanium shortages, dropping CPI to 0.97, but a recovery plan with additive manufacturing for airframes aims for breakeven CPI by Q1 2025.

Missiles and Precision Weapons, 30% of the segment, led with 14.1% margins—up 120 basis points—powered by hypersonic Glide Phase Interceptor hitting FRP with CPI at 1.12 from JASSM-ER ramps. We offset 3% inflation in titanium and energetics via forward buys and dual-sourcing, while Ukraine and Red Sea issues spurred $2.1 billion in FY24 orders. FMS to Poland and Saudi Arabia raised international mix to 28%, with margins 200 basis points higher on CPFF terms.

Space Systems margins dipped to 9.8% from 10.4% on $120 million overruns for Orion-like crew vehicle propulsion revalidation after SLS Artemis I, with SPI at 0.94 from NASA changes, but fixed-price caps exposure at 5%. Commercial LEO like NovaStar ramped to 11.5% margins via reusable launches akin to Starship. US Space Force GPS III Follow-On stayed on track, offset EMEA ESA cuts.

Commercial Aviation at 15% saw margins at 8.7% from 9.5% due to 787-style bottlenecks on widebody composites and $30 million from Pratt GTF delays, CPI at 0.96. Aftermarket MRO up 12% added 150 basis points, with A320neo APAC ahead, China at 18% backlog.

Cost trends showed inflation-adjusted sales costs up 6% YoY versus 7-8% guide, via AeroLean 2.0 AI analytics on 25 programs saving $250 million annually, including 20% touch labor cuts via cobots. Supply chain secured 85% critical commodities with multi-year deals against Red Sea issues. Engineer retention at 92% with incentives.

For margin growth, we shifted to 65% FFP/FPI from 55%, digital thread for 100-150 bps by 2026, and international at 35% backlog with premium terms from Indo-Pacific needs. Q4 margins guide 11.5-12.0%, FY24 11.0% up 70 bps, FY25 12.0%+. Backlog $28 billion 60% funded buffers DoD CR and election risks.

Building on this execution, let's discuss our major new contract awards and program wins, which mark a pivotal advancement for Aether Dynamics. These successes highlight our tech edge in core A&D areas and lock in revenue visibility plus margin upside amid global tensions from Ukraine and Middle East to Indo-Pacific, with SIPRI noting 6.8% YoY defense spend growth to $2.4 trillion in 2023, mid-single digits through 2028 on NGAD, hypersonics, C4ISR.

Fixed-wing took 45% of bookings: a $4.2 billion IDIQ from USAF for Lot 18 F-35 wing assemblies and mission upgrades, ceiling $6 billion options, ramping 240 sets/year by FY26 with Block 4 sensor fusion, EW resilience—F-35 content now 12%, margins to 14-15% in FRP.

Plus $1.8 billion FMS for F-35 fuselages for 28 NATO jets, Poland/Germany; Europe backlog $12.4 billion up 28%, €500 million annual exports on AUKUS/NATO 2%.

Hypersonics/strategic missiles, 35% CAGR: $2.9 billion CPIF with Army RCCTO for 120 Glide Phase Interceptor rounds, Mach 7+ 1500km, post-TRL7 White Sands, better than ARRW on composites; FY24 $1.1 billion funded, to $15 billion family by 2028, Japan/Australia interest.

Directed energy/missile defense: $1.5 billion sole-source MDA for 50 300kW HEL turrets on Strykers IFPC Inc2, 30 shots/min <1¢ vs PAC-3; $950 million UAE FMS Patriot GEM-T with GaN AESA amid Houthis; Middle East backlog $8.2 billion up 42% Abraham Accords.

Space: $3.1 billion USSF for 36 PWSA ESS sats, laser-linked Ka-band 10x Milstar, Vulcan refuel 2025.

Total $14.35 billion bookings, 1.7x book-to-bill, funded backlog $52.7 billion up 32%, 65% funded 40% next 24 months; unfunded $28.4 billion IDIQ like F-35 pool. New win margins 13.2% +200bps on fixed-price, 85% suppliers domestic/AUKUS CHIPS.

Strategy: disaggregated lethality, AI autonomy ViperEdge swarms, legacy upgrades; 4.5% sales R&D hypersonics/space awareness, FY25 DoD $145 billion procurement; $180 billion pipeline 60% win prob NGAD/FLRAA.

These secure FY24 12-15% revenue to $28-30 billion, 15.5-16.5% EBITDA.

Next, our updated full-year 2024 guidance. We refine it upward from January, on H1 execution, awards, ramps. Revenue now $32.5-34.0 billion from $30.5-32.5 billion, 12-15% YoY midpoint from defense/space acceleration. Adjusted diluted EPS $14.20-15.00 from $13.00-14.00, ~18% growth midpoint, better fixed-price, supply efficiencies.

By segment:

Defense Electronics/Missiles (52%): $17.0-17.8 billion from $16.2-17.0; hypersonic glide (HAWC-like) $2.4 billion USAF, PSM 150/month Huntsville AM; NATO PSM-F-35 Poland/Finland $1.1 billion; margins 14.5-15.5% +150bps learning/labor.

Combat Aircraft/Sustainment (28%): $9.2-9.7 from $8.8-9.3; F-35 Lot16 LRIP avionics/sensors; F-15EX EW pod $850 million; ME sustain Saudi/UAE, 1.4x btb; 12.0-13.0%.

Space (15%): $4.8-5.2 from $4.5-4.9; pLEO bus NRO $1.2 billion resilient comms; ULA Vulcan; hypersonic reentry Q4 Mayhem; 13.5-14.5%.

Commercial Aviation (5%): $1.5 billion hold, widebody lag narrowbody; defense priority.

Consolidated margins 13.8-14.8% +120bps, 8% inflation via ERP/AI; FCF $3.8-4.2 billion, $1.2 billion repurchases, 1.8% yield.

US DoD +6% FY24; Pacific 20%+ Japan/Australia China; Europe NATO $3.5 billion pipeline. Risks titanium/Ukraine, labor composites, CR; $102 billion backlog up 7% QoQ 35% funded 24 months.

Digital twins NGAD 6th-gen 2026, counter-drone FalconEye Anduril-lattice; $1.1 trillion A&D to 2030 Teal.

Now, detailed revenue and earnings guidance by segment for FY24 and 2025 preview. Total revenue raised to $72.5-74.5 billion from $70-72 billion, op profit $11.2-11.6 billion 15.3-15.6% margins; F-35 lot pricing, CH-53K, $2.1 billion commercial engines; 1.15x btb $125 billion backlog.

Commercial Aerospace (28% Q3): $20.5-21.0 billion +22% YoY from $19.5-20.5; profit $3.4-3.6 billion 16.5-17.1% from 15.8%; 737 MAX 38/month LEAP-1B; MRO +15% GE9X TBO; NA 60% APAC 25% CAGR IndiGo/Air India A320neo; $450 million digital/AM winglets +200bps 2026; Boeing risk low Spirit expo; 2025 18-20%.

Defense Systems (42%): $30.0-30.8 +8% from $29-30; profit $4.6-4.8 15.3-15.6%; F-35 55% Lot18 $80M/jet 156 deliv vs 142; Poland/Finland +30%; HAWC hypersonic DARPA $1.2 billion Q2'25 flight; 1.2x btb Ukraine $61B; DoD 70% ME Patriot +25% Europe 18% IndoPac AUKUS; NGAD Northrop EMD 2026; 2025 10% 16.2% $850B DoD.

Rotary/Mission (18%): $13.0-13.4 flat-+3%; profit $1.9-2.0 14.6-14.9%; CH-53K 12/year USMC IOC UH-60M $800M; AN/APY-9 E-7 $900M USAF AWACS; 45% US 30% int Saudi MH-60R; ti rotors -20% lead AI PM GE twin 300h MTBF; 2025 7-9% MH-139.

Space (12%): $9.0-9.3 +14%; profit $1.3-1.4 14.4-15.0%; Artemis II Sep'25 ESC-D Vulcan 38 miss; Starlink payloads $500M hypersonic reentry; LEO 25% CAGR backlog $18B double; 65% US NRO/SDA 20% comm Blue/SpaceX; $300M laser R&D Tranche3; 2025 20% 15.5%.

Raised guide execution resilient portfolio defense offsets commercial; 2025 $78-81B 9-12% geo/commercial.

Wrapping financials with revenue drivers and headwinds analysis. Q4 revenue $6.2 billion +14% YoY full $24.7B, +5% guide mid; 1.25x btb backlog $158B +18%.

Defense (62% $9.8B equiv) +16% YoY: geo NATO/IndoPac; F-35 sustain $1.54B equiv +22% Block4 AESA/EW; DoD $11.5B NDAA Japan 42/jet Poland 32 Fort Worth/Greenville full.

Missiles/hypo +28% $510M equiv Army $2.1B IDIQ AGM-183A Navy CPS; AM SRM -35% lead +20% marg; Europe 25% +7pts AUKUS Aus sub $800M Q4.

Commercial (28% $6.8B equiv but 15% adj) +9% accel: PW1100G OEM $280M A320neo 55/month Cirium; aftermarket +16% $310M digital twin CFM56/LEAP -22% downtime Delta/United; APAC IndiGo 500+ $150M serv 45% mix vs 35% '22.

Space/Adv (10%): +20% Artemis Orion prop Starshield; NSSL3 $1.2B Space Force 15+ Vulcan Q3 fairings/stages ULA.

Capex $450M wind tunnels AI supply; M&A $320M UK UAV counter-UAS Red Sea.

Headwinds: supply $120M ti Russia/Ukraine +45% spot dual Japan/US 18mo -15%; FAA GTF dur A320neo Q4 defer $90M OEM serv offset; infla/forex 3-4% -80bps 12.2%; labor 8% Okla upskill $50M Tulsa; China rare earth avionics 15% shift MP Mat; US aid fatigue 8-10% FY25 ME Patriot +$600M accel.

FY24 reaffirm $26-27B Q4 def +18%; FCF $3.5B div +2.5% $1.8B repurchase; 60/30/10 resilient Boeing/Lockheed GAO F-35 overruns.

Fortress Forward: harden supply scale hypo space comm. 

In Q4 specifically, we reported revenue of $6.2 billion, up 14% year-over-year. Adjusted EPS was $3.10. We generated strong free cash flow of $850 million in the quarter. Balance sheet remains robust with $4.8 billion in cash and equivalents. Full-year guidance for 2024 is now $26.0 billion to $27.0 billion in revenue and $13.50 to $14.00 adjusted EPS, unchanged at midpoint but with conviction. Gross margin expanded to 13.8%, operating income $3.4 billion full year, free cash flow $3.2 billion. We're managing costs tightly while investing in growth, and committed to capital returns via dividends and repurchases.

John Ellis:
Thank you, Sarah. Operationally, we've made major strides in supply chain oversight, boosting production rates on flagship programs like F-47 and hypersonics. Our Resilient Supply Chain 2.0 localized critical parts, yielding $450 million savings, while AeroLean 2.0 digital tools and cobotic lines cut labor 20% and lead times. Factories now run digital threads for 18% productivity gains, positioning us for FY24 ramps.

Dr. Lisa Chen:
Thank you, John. Technologically, we're advancing next-generation propulsion, including Glide Phase Interceptor hypersonics at Mach 7+ with superior thermal composites, and NGAD digital twins reducing ECOs 15%. Directed energy HELs at 300kW for IFPC, laser comms for PWSA sats, and AI autonomy for swarms give us enduring edges. These, plus $1.2 billion R&D, secure leadership in 6th-gen and beyond.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Josh Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Josh Smith:
Good morning, team. Can you provide more color on the major new contract awards and how they impact backlog conversion?

Mark Harlan:
Certainly, Josh. These $14.35 billion wins, like the $4.2 billion F-35 IDIQ and $2.9 billion GPI hypersonic, drive 1.7x book-to-bill, pushing funded backlog to $52.7 billion with 40% converting in 24 months. Margins richer at 13.2%, de-risking 12-15% growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about risks to the updated full-year guidance, particularly supply chain and commercial?

Sarah Thompson:
Emily, our raised $32.5-34 billion revenue and $14.20-15.00 EPS bake in titanium derisks via dual-sourcing and $102 billion backlog visibility. Commercial at $1.5 billion prioritizes defense stability, with aftermarket offsetting OEM delays—confident in delivery.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Thanks. Regarding the program margins and cost performance, any updates on inflation mitigation?

Dr. Lisa Chen:
David, our 11.2% Q4 margins reflect CPI/SPI outperformance on NGAD at 1.05/1.02, with AeroLean AI saving $250 million annualized. Fixed-price shift to 65%, digital thread add 100-150 bps by 2026—FY24 11.0%, FY25 12%+ on track.

Mark Harlan:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Fourth Quarter and Full-Year 2023 Earnings Conference Call. A replay will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
